boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From signing a class banner to breakfast served by faculty during finals, these documented Forester traditions mark the Lake Forest College calendar.

cards.title: Meet Your Class at Full Speed
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation team-building tradition
cards.notes: Join the incoming class for guided games and team exercises; consult the Orientation schedule for your assigned session.
cards.short_summary: A high-energy introduction built around games with new classmates.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College identifies Playfair! as a New Student Orientation staple where first-year and transfer students bond through games and activities.
cards.access_notes: Intended for participating new first-year and transfer students during New Student Orientation; follow the official schedule.

cards.title: Start College Beside Lake Michigan
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation at Lake Forest Beach
cards.notes: Bring activity-ready clothing and follow College swimming and paddling instructions; confirm transportation in the Orientation schedule.
cards.short_summary: New Foresters close Orientation with outdoor recreation by the lake.
cards.evidence_claim: The College documents Beach Bash as an Orientation event where new first-year and transfer students play beach games, swim, and kayak on Lake Michigan.
cards.access_notes: Orientation programming for new students; activities and transportation are schedule-dependent and may be weather-dependent.

cards.title: Take the First-Year Classroom to Chicago
cards.subtitle: Fall-semester excursion before classes begin
cards.notes: Check your First-Year Studies instructions for the destination and meeting point; each professor organizes a class-specific trip.
cards.short_summary: First-year seminars explore Chicago together before the semester starts.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College calls Chicago Day a fall tradition held the day before classes, with First-Year Studies professors organizing class trips into Chicago.
cards.access_notes: Designed for first-year students through their First-Year Studies classes; destinations and travel details vary by class.

cards.title: Put Your Name on the Class Banner
cards.subtitle: A long-standing new-student ritual at Patterson Lodge
cards.notes: Follow Orientation leaders to the signing line and add your name when directed; the banner represents the entering class.
cards.short_summary: Incoming students sign a shared banner before formally joining the College community.
cards.evidence_claim: An official College account describes signing the Matriculation Banner at Patterson Lodge as a long-standing tradition for new Lake Forest College students.
cards.access_notes: Part of scheduled new-student Matriculation programming; current timing and procession details should be confirmed through Orientation.

cards.title: Walk Through a Wall of Forester Cheers
cards.subtitle: The community welcome after Matriculation
cards.notes: Exit with your class and proceed through the cheering route as directed; spectators should use the announced viewing area.
cards.short_summary: The Forester community forms a cheering passage for newly matriculated students.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College documents a Matriculation custom in which faculty, staff, students, and other Foresters form a cheering gauntlet for the entering class.
cards.access_notes: The walk is tied to the scheduled Matriculation ceremony; current route and spectator arrangements may change.

cards.title: Turn Friday Red and Black
cards.subtitle: Weekly Forester spirit-wear tradition
cards.notes: Wear Lake Forest College clothing or red and black on Friday; watch for the fall kickoff event on the Middle Campus Quad.
cards.short_summary: Friday becomes the recurring day for Forester colors and College apparel.
cards.evidence_claim: The College states that community members wear Lake Forest College clothing or red and black during Forester Fridays and holds an annual fall kickoff.
cards.access_notes: The clothing custom recurs on Fridays; the kickoff event date and offerings are announced separately by the College.

cards.title: Gather Around the Homecoming Fire
cards.subtitle: An annual Homecoming and Reunion Weekend event
cards.notes: Use only the official gathering area and follow event staff directions; verify the Homecoming schedule before heading out.
cards.short_summary: Students and returning alumni gather for the annual Homecoming bonfire.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College identifies the annual bonfire as part of Homecoming and Reunion Weekend, alongside reunions and the Forester football game.
cards.access_notes: Attend only as part of the supervised official Homecoming program; date, location, and weather status are schedule-dependent.

cards.title: Let Faculty Serve the Finals Fuel
cards.subtitle: Semesterly breakfast in the Caf during finals
cards.notes: Check the finals-week announcement, then arrive at the Caf for the scheduled evening service led by volunteering faculty and staff.
cards.short_summary: Breakfast food arrives at night, served by familiar campus faces during finals.
cards.evidence_claim: The College describes Late Night Breakfast as a semesterly finals-week event where faculty and staff serve breakfast classics beginning at 9 p.m. in the Caf.
cards.access_notes: The cited College description gives a 9 p.m. start during finals week; confirm the current semester's date and meal-access rules.

cards.title: Share the Cultures of the Forest
cards.subtitle: Fall signature event for the campus community
cards.notes: Look for the fall event announcement, then attend ready to explore student and community cultural stories respectfully.
cards.short_summary: The campus gathers each fall around the cultures represented within its community.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College lists Global Fest as a fall signature event celebrating the cultures and traditions represented across campus and open to the College community.
cards.access_notes: Open to members of the Lake Forest College community; consult the current fall announcement for date, venue, and participation details.

cards.title: Seat Students With 51-Years-Out Alumni
cards.subtitle: A new Homecoming tradition across generations
cards.notes: Eligible alumni should follow Homecoming registration; invited students can arrive prepared to exchange College stories across generations.
cards.short_summary: Longtime alumni and current students meet over a Homecoming meal.
cards.evidence_claim: The College calls the annual Golden Foresters Luncheon a new tradition for alumni who graduated 51 or more years ago and documents student participation in 2025.
cards.source_title: Golden Foresters Luncheon celebrates lifelong connections across generations
cards.access_notes: Homecoming event for qualifying alumni and invited student participants; registration or invitation requirements may apply.
